So far so good. They work in my Keurig 2.0 machine. I just have to figure out the best grind for them and my desired coffee strength using a burr grinder.

TIPS
* Use a burr grinder; don't use a blade grinder (can't control grind well and creates too much "coffee dust")
* Don't pack grinds in too much or it can obstruct water flow and cause problems
* To empty, keep lid closed, turn upside down on counter and tap a few times, then open the lid over the garbage and grinds usually just fall out... then rinse with water.

I like the purple pod and LOVE the orange one.
The purple pod works differently than the orange one in two ways.
1. The purple pod works like a traditional sized k-cup. This means the needle that puntures the k cups is present. If you are not careful, you can poke the mesh, which has happened to mine more than once. These holes are permanent and grounds do come through them.
2. The purple k-cup takes you directly to the k-cup menu which means you are reduced to selecting the 6oz. or 8oz serving sized. It holds very little coffee so this makes sense.

The orange cup has a hard plastic bottom, when it is inserted the needle ment for puncturing slides away so holes on the bottom are not a risk. The orange on also give you access to the full menu of the kuerig where you can select larger portions.
I use a dark roast, expresso ground coffee and I find that at max, this pod fits about .75 oz. of coffee which for me tastes best at 14oz. after which I add about 4 oz. of milk.
As you may be able to tell, I perfer the orange pod, but having both is convenient as I am not the only coffee drinker in my household.
